summary.oneLiner: Cummins India is a high-payout, net-cash market leader riding a structural domestic power-gen upcycle, with **data-center gensets (30–35% of domestic powergen)** as the marquee growth driver on top of CPCB-IV+ content gains, a fast-growing 20%+ distribution/aftermarket annuity, and a steady-but-cautious export book — guidance for FY27 is deliberately "moderate growth across segments" given commodity inflation and geopolitics.
summary.business: Cummins India Limited manufactures internal combustion engines (non-vehicular), generator sets, and engine/turbine parts and accessories, and provides parts, service and aftermarket support for gensets and related technologies through its Power Systems Business Unit (PSBU) and Distribution Business Unit (DBU). It serves OEMs, end users, and channel partners (dealers, distributors, retailers) across power generation and industrial end markets including railways, mining, marine, oil & gas, defence, construction and pumps in India, Bhutan and Nepal, and exports to about 86 countries including the US, Europe, Mexico, Africa, the Middle East and China.

Railways: CPCB IV+ compliant Power Car diesel alternator (DA) sets
Engines for Track Maintenance Machines and Shunting locomotives
Propulsion systems for High-Speed Self-Propelled Accident Relief Trains (HSSPART) and Self-Propelled Inspection Cars (SPIC)
Marine: Engines and generator sets for Green Tugs, Multi-Purpose Vessels, Offshore Patrol Vessels, Ocean Research Vessels, Fleet Support Ships and Submarine applications
Mining: Engines for Heavy Earth Moving Machinery (HEMM), dump trucks, underground mine trucks, motor graders, dozers and stone crushers
Defence: Engines for Advanced Towed Artillery Gun Systems and Light Tanks (wheeled and tracked platforms)
Pumps: FMUL high-speed engines (High Horsepower / HHP range)
Construction: Engines for construction and earthmoving equipment; CEV BS V compliant product portfolio

currentContext.expansion: Capacity and footprint additions during FY26 were largely product/technology and channel expansion rather than named new plants. R&D new-product development included: a horizontal engine developed for the High-Speed Self-Propelled Accident Relief Train (HSSPART) application; a large-size 95L product developed for Marine power generation for a Navy fleet support ship; an export-ready Euro Stage V compliant product line introduced for the EU market (exports commenced); a CPCBIV+ norm range 82.5 kVA product with the X3.7 engine certified and launched; QSM15 Chile phase-II LPO units shipped to the LATAM region leveraging CPCBIV+ architecture; the genset test facility was upgraded with advanced safety standards and integrated controls; a new bench testing rig was introduced for cylinder block buster testing to support development of India-manufactured blocks for global use; and CEV BS V emission rollout was carried out for Construction Equipment Vehicles along with Trem IV/V for combined harvesters. On the renewable/energy side, the Kothrud Engine Plant (KEP) implemented Solar Phase VI, comprising a 160 kWp PV car-port installation, alongside continued offsite procurement of solar and wind power, taking KEP's cumulative installed solar capacity to 4,400 kWp. Channel footprint was expanded with 12 additional sales dealers added across geographies and the GOEM dealer network growing from 117 (FY25) to 133 (FY26). The Cummins Technical Training Center in Phaltan hosted its first-ever global training batch for Cummins Arabia. R&D future plans (per the Directors' Report) include technological innovation in alternate fuels, power electronics, battery energy storage systems, microgrid and hybrid engines; continued expansion of the product range for local and global markets; and continued focus on indigenization and supplier waste-elimination initiatives.

risks.risk: Export demand concentration and trade-policy risk
risks.note: The Company's export growth continues to be linked to demand conditions in key partner geographies; the escalation in global trade tensions during FY 2025-26 has created a more complex environment for export-oriented businesses.

risks.risk: Uneven private capex recovery / global industrial cycle risk
risks.note: While private capital investment showed improvement in FY 2025-26 versus prior years, the pace of private capex recovery remains uneven across sectors; any slowdown in the global industrial cycle could have knock-on effects on domestic capital goods demand, on which the Company's Industrial and PowerGen businesses depend.

Management has explicitly identified climate action as a material sustainability issue presenting risk or opportunity to the Company's business, per the risks and concerns disclosure in the MD&A (detailed further in the BRSR).

Management has explicitly identified cybersecurity as a material sustainability issue presenting risk to the Company's business; the Risk Management Committee's oversight mandate explicitly includes overseeing that cyber security risks are identified and assessed.

risks.risk: Segment concentration in Rail within Industrial Markets
risks.note: The Rail segment has been the largest contributor to the overall revenues of the domestic Industrial Markets business, making the Company's Industrial performance sensitive to Indian Railways' procurement timing and scale.

risks.risk: Supply chain fragility / supplier financial health
risks.note: The Company is actively managing supply-chain risk via dual sourcing, adjusted payment terms with financially weaker suppliers, price revisions, long-term supplier agreements and inventory building where necessary — indicating an acknowledged exposure to supply disruption and weaker-supplier risk.

**Full-year FY26 (vs FY25):**
| Metric | FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | ₹11,950 cr | +18% | from ₹10,166 cr |

| PBT (pre-exceptional) | ₹3,104 cr | +24% | margin-accretive growth |
| PBT (post-exceptional) | ₹3,054 cr | +22% | exceptional ≈ -₹50 cr (FY) |

**FY26 domestic segment split:**
- Power Generation: ₹4,758 cr (+24%)
- Distribution: ₹3,278 cr (+22%)
- Industrial: ₹1,650 cr (-1%, marginally lower)

**Q4 FY26 (vs Q4 FY25 / vs Q3 FY26):**
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | ₹2,963 cr | +23% | -1% | vs ₹2,414 cr YoY; ₹3,006 cr QoQ |
| Domestic | ₹2,513 cr | +30% | -1% | |
| Exports | ₹450 cr | -6% | -5% | weak vs strong base |
| PBT (pre-exc.) | ₹820 cr | +20% | +14% | |
| PBT (post-exc.) | ₹852 cr | +25% | +44% | Q4 exceptional ≈ +₹32 cr (gain) |

**Q4 FY26 segment split (domestic):**
- Power Generation: ₹1,294 cr (+48% YoY, +21% QoQ) — strongest engine
- Distribution: ₹766 cr (+21% YoY, -18% QoQ)
- Industrial: ₹381 cr (+1% YoY, -18% QoQ)
- Exports HHP: ₹217 cr (-1% YoY, -7% QoQ); LHP: ₹127 cr (-18% YoY, -5% QoQ)

**Q4 powergen sub-split:** LHP ₹55 cr; medium-range ₹177 cr; heavy-duty ₹108 cr; remainder HHP (~₹954 cr, of which Hyperscaler ≈ ₹250 cr).
**Q4 industrial sub-split:** construction ₹164 cr; rail ₹111 cr; compressor ₹59 cr; remainder mining + defence.

**One-offs / quality flags:** Growth described as **predominantly volume-led** (mgmt: CPCB-IV+ price/content add is part, but HHP + industrial + distribution make it "actually volume led growth"). CPCB-IV+ prebuy not flagged as a one-off this quarter; transition now stable. Exceptional items small (-₹50 cr FY / +₹32 cr Q4 implied). Net-cash balance sheet (not quantified on call; structurally cash-rich, no major capex plan).
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue growth FY27:** "Moderate growth across segments" — explicitly NOT quantified; mgmt declined low-double-digit / mid-teens / high-single-digit framing. Domestic demand "robust" (inquiries + order book), but cautious on commodity inflation + geopolitics.
- **Margin:** No explicit margin guidance. Mgmt insists data-center/CPCB-IV+ growth is NOT materially margin-dilutive because localization content is "already very high" even on imported-engine products; pricing "largely sustaining" post CPCB-IV+ (30–35% price hike absorbed). HHP range positioned as higher-value.
- **Export outlook:** Cautious — "difficult to put fingers down" given geopolitics. Europe + Asia-Pac growing modestly; Middle East & others soft. No structural change in trend.
- **Data-center demand:** Very strong. ≈30–35% of domestic powergen (FY26), ~35% Q4. Inquiry velocity up sharply since Oct-2025, led by Colo, with Hyperscalers also building. Near-term (2–3 yrs) demand from Colo stays on localized QSK60 — clear line of sight. Installed base view referenced: ~1.5GW → 6–10GW potential. Order-to-delivery ~6–12 months before site ready; revenue recognized on genset installation.
demand / pipeline:
- Domestic demand "robust" across powergen/industrial/distribution; order book strong.
- Data center inquiry velocity sharply up since Oct-2025 (Colo > Hyperscalers, but both growing); large competitor orders being finalized (Perkins, Baudouin, Adani referenced by analyst).
- Non-data-center powergen demand: solar-cell manufacturing plants, pharma, quick-commerce dark stores, luxury residential & commercial realty — all showing good inquiries/orders. Non-DC powergen grew "higher double digits" in FY26.
- Industrial: railways performing very well (good order book); mining picked up last 6 months (tender velocity recovering); construction moderate (road-construction-linked); compressor entering cyclical down-leg.
segment commentary:
- **PowerGen (₹4,758 cr FY, +24%):** Star segment, data-center-led + broad-based (manufacturing, pharma, realty, quick-commerce). Q4 +48% YoY. Data center 30–35% of domestic powergen.
- **Industrial (₹1,650 cr FY, -1%):** Soft full-year; rail strong & sustaining, mining recovering, construction moderate, compressor down-cycle.
- **Distribution / aftermarket (₹3,278 cr FY, +22%):** Growth solutions-led, NOT price-led — service packages, predictive maintenance, dual-fuel kits, retrofit emission devices, parts beyond engines. CPCB-IV+ engines coming out of warranty from June onwards = annuity opportunity via extended-warranty schemes. Separate dedicated data-center aftermarket focus (99.99% uptime) over-and-above the 30–35% powergen DC number (not quantified).
- **Exports (₹1,989 cr FY, +12%):** HHP ₹984 cr (+20%); LHP ₹807 cr (+3%). Europe/Asia-Pac modest growth; Middle East soft. India base used for component sourcing into global DC engine builds.
growth / optionality:
- **Data-center HHP gensets:** QSK60 (localized) dominant for next 2–3 yrs; may shift toward 78L (more likely) and 95L over time — would re-evaluate India localization as volumes build. 95L not made by anyone in India (all imported, built in US).
- **Parent capacity:** Cummins Inc. investing ~$450m to add ~20GW capacity by 2030 (DC-focused) → expected to crunch import lead-times for QSK78/95 (lead-times have risen materially given global DC demand).
- **Exports leverage:** India supply base sourced into global DC builds.
- **New fuels / BESS:** Strong interest & inquiries in Battery Energy Storage Systems but no meaningful sales yet; NO local supply chain (import-dependent today), working on localization; positive long-term outlook, contribution un-quantifiable. Parent's gas/peak-shaving prime-mover product seen as US-specific — NOT an India opportunity. Other allied power solutions under evaluation (nothing to share yet).
margins & cost:
- Margins protected — high localization content even on imported-engine DC/CPCB-IV+ products; data-center/CPCB-IV+ growth "not impacting margins dramatically."
- Commodity inflation a headwind (incl. ~doubling of DEF / Diesel Exhaust Fluid prices, though DEF a very small share of distribution). Price hikes passed on with a lag and friction; CPCB-IV+ 30–35% price increase has sustained.
- Industry-wide supply constraints: supplier labour shortages, fuel-cost increments, war-related logistics delays.
capex: - Capacity utilization ~70% (combined powergen+industrial facilities). NO major capex plan; >₹1,000 cr invested over last 5 years on modernization + line-capability expansion (more output per line). Global integrated supply chain tapped for incremental output. Asset-light growth via productivity, not big greenfield.
capital allocation: - Structurally net-cash, high-payout profile (consistent with history; not explicitly quantified on this call). Continuous modest capex; no large outlay planned. (Dividend specifics not discussed on call.)
risks:
- Commodity inflation + DEF cost spikes; pass-through lag on pre-booked orders.
- Geopolitical / war-driven logistics delays and uncertainty (esp. exports).
- Demand elasticity below HHP (CPCB-IV+ range, short lead-times) if inflation worsens — HHP/project demand stays inelastic.
- Long-term mix shift to imported 78L/95L DC engines could narrow Cummins' localization cost-advantage vs peers (Perkins, Baudouin) all on imports — though mgmt argues whole-solution value proposition, not price, wins.
- Rising lead-times on imported nodes/engines due to global DC demand outpacing capacity.
- Competition poaching senior talent from Cummins (mgmt downplays).
management tone: Confident and measured. Bullish on domestic/data-center structural demand and distribution annuity; deliberately conservative on FY27 ("moderate growth," repeated caution on commodities/geopolitics). Guarded on quantification — declined to give DC sub-revenue, currency-depreciation split, lead-time numbers, BESS contribution, exact margins. Emphasizes value-proposition / end-to-end solution moat over pure price competition.
non-obvious insights:
- India DC share of powergen (30–35%) is structured differently from parent's "25%" (parent number is share of broader business, not powergen-only; parent's powergen-only DC share is much higher). India DC market only started accelerating Oct-2025; US/China far ahead — big optionality if India catches up.
- CPCB-IV+ engines exiting warranty (from June 2026) = new high-margin distribution/aftermarket annuity ("encircle the customer," extended-warranty schemes) on sophisticated after-treatment tech.
- Hyperscaler revenue Q4 ≈ ₹250 cr (vs implied HHP ~₹954 cr) — Colo still the bigger driver.
- Luxury-residential realty growth does NOT lift per-unit backup-power intensity — stays "backup," no scale change in utilization.
- BESS is import-dependent with no local supply chain yet — a gap vs the structural BESS push in India.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ **Data-center buildout (Colo + Hyperscaler):** Cummins India direct beneficiary via QSK60/HHP gensets + dedicated DC aftermarket.
- ✅ **CPCB-IV+ out-of-warranty wave (Jun-2026 onward):** boosts distribution/aftermarket annuity.
- ⭐ **Parent's 20GW / $450m capacity add by 2030:** could shorten import lead-times → faster India DC fulfilment, but also enables imported 78/95L that may pressure local cost-edge.
- ⭐ **Solar-cell / pharma / quick-commerce / realty capex:** secondary powergen demand pools.

---

FY26 sales ₹11,950 cr (+18%), PBT pre-exc ₹3,104 cr (+24%). FY27 guidance: "moderate growth across segments," cautious on commodities/geopolitics. Util ~70%, no major capex. BESS interest but no sales/local supply. CPCB-IV+ out-of-warranty annuity emerging from Jun-2026.

Mgmt insists data-center/CPCB-IV+ growth is NOT materially margin-dilutive because localization content is "already very high" even on imported-engine products; pricing "largely sustaining" post CPCB-IV+ (30–35% price hike absorbed). HHP range positioned as higher-value.
- **Export outlook:** Cautious — "difficult to put fingers down" given geopolitics. Europe + Asia-Pac growing modestly; Middle East & others soft. No structural change in trend.
- **Data-center demand:** Very strong. ≈30–35% of domestic powergen (FY26), ~35% Q4. Inquiry velocity up sharply since Oct-2025, led by Colo, with Hyperscalers also building. Near-term (2–3 yrs) demand from Colo stays on localized QSK60 — clear line of sight. Installed base view referenced: ~1.5GW → 6–10GW potential. Order-to-delivery ~6–12 months before site ready; revenue recognized on genset installation.
demand / pipeline:
- Domestic demand "robust" across powergen/industrial/distribution; order book strong.
- Data center inquiry velocity sharply up since Oct-2025 (Colo > Hyperscalers, but both growing); large competitor orders being finalized (Perkins, Baudouin, Adani referenced by analyst).
- Non-data-center powergen demand: solar-cell manufacturing plants, pharma, quick-commerce dark stores, luxury residential & commercial realty — all showing good inquiries/orders. Non-DC powergen grew "higher double digits" in FY26.
- Industrial: railways performing very well (good order book); mining picked up last 6 months (tender velocity recovering); construction moderate (road-construction-linked); compressor entering cyclical down-leg.
segment commentary:
- **PowerGen (₹4,758 cr FY, +24%):** Star segment, data-center-led + broad-based (manufacturing, pharma, realty, quick-commerce). Q4 +48% YoY. Data center 30–35% of domestic powergen.
- **Industrial (₹1,650 cr FY, -1%):** Soft full-year; rail strong & sustaining, mining recovering, construction moderate, compressor down-cycle.
- **Distribution / aftermarket (₹3,278 cr FY, +22%):** Growth solutions-led, NOT price-led — service packages, predictive maintenance, dual-fuel kits, retrofit emission devices, parts beyond engines. CPCB-IV+ engines coming out of warranty from June onwards = annuity opportunity via extended-warranty schemes. Separate dedicated data-center aftermarket focus (99.99% uptime) over-and-above the 30–35% powergen DC number (not quantified).
- **Exports (₹1,989 cr FY, +12%):** HHP ₹984 cr (+20%); LHP ₹807 cr (+3%). Europe/Asia-Pac modest growth; Middle East soft. India base used for component sourcing into global DC engine builds.
growth / optionality:
- **Data-center HHP gensets:** QSK60 (localized) dominant for next 2–3 yrs; may shift toward 78L (more likely) and 95L over time — would re-evaluate India localization as volumes build. 95L not made by anyone in India (all imported, built in US).
- **Parent capacity:** Cummins Inc. investing ~$450m to add ~20GW capacity by 2030 (DC-focused) → expected to crunch import lead-times for QSK78/95 (lead-times have risen materially given global DC demand).
- **Exports leverage:** India supply base sourced into global DC builds.
- **New fuels / BESS:** Strong interest & inquiries in Battery Energy Storage Systems but no meaningful sales yet; NO local supply chain (import-dependent today), working on localization; positive long-term outlook, contribution un-quantifiable. Parent's gas/peak-shaving prime-mover product seen as US-specific — NOT an India opportunity. Other allied power solutions under evaluation (nothing to share yet).
margins & cost:
- Margins protected — high localization content even on imported-engine DC/CPCB-IV+ products; data-center/CPCB-IV+ growth "not impacting margins dramatically."
- Commodity inflation a headwind (incl. ~doubling of DEF / Diesel Exhaust Fluid prices, though DEF a very small share of distribution). Price hikes passed on with a lag and friction; CPCB-IV+ 30–35% price increase has sustained.
- Industry-wide supply constraints: supplier labour shortages, fuel-cost increments, war-related logistics delays.
capex: - Capacity utilization ~70% (combined powergen+industrial facilities). NO major capex plan; >₹1,000 cr invested over last 5 years on modernization + line-capability expansion (more output per line). Global integrated supply chain tapped for incremental output. Asset-light growth via productivity, not big greenfield.
capital allocation: - Structurally net-cash, high-payout profile (consistent with history; not explicitly quantified on this call). Continuous modest capex; no large outlay planned. (Dividend specifics not discussed on call.)
risks:
- Commodity inflation + DEF cost spikes; pass-through lag on pre-booked orders.
- Geopolitical / war-driven logistics delays and uncertainty (esp. exports).
- Demand elasticity below HHP (CPCB-IV+ range, short lead-times) if inflation worsens — HHP/project demand stays inelastic.
- Long-term mix shift to imported 78L/95L DC engines could narrow Cummins' localization cost-advantage vs peers (Perkins, Baudouin) all on imports — though mgmt argues whole-solution value proposition, not price, wins.
- Rising lead-times on imported nodes/engines due to global DC demand outpacing capacity.
- Competition poaching senior talent from Cummins (mgmt downplays).
management tone: Confident and measured. Bullish on domestic/data-center structural demand and distribution annuity; deliberately conservative on FY27 ("moderate growth," repeated caution on commodities/geopolitics). Guarded on quantification — declined to give DC sub-revenue, currency-depreciation split, lead-time numbers, BESS contribution, exact margins. Emphasizes value-proposition / end-to-end solution moat over pure price competition.
non-obvious insights:
- India DC share of powergen (30–35%) is structured differently from parent's "25%" (parent number is share of broader business, not powergen-only; parent's powergen-only DC share is much higher). India DC market only started accelerating Oct-2025; US/China far ahead — big optionality if India catches up.
- CPCB-IV+ engines exiting warranty (from June 2026) = new high-margin distribution/aftermarket annuity ("encircle the customer," extended-warranty schemes) on sophisticated after-treatment tech.
- Hyperscaler revenue Q4 ≈ ₹250 cr (vs implied HHP ~₹954 cr) — Colo still the bigger driver.
- Luxury-residential realty growth does NOT lift per-unit backup-power intensity — stays "backup," no scale change in utilization.
- BESS is import-dependent with no local supply chain yet — a gap vs the structural BESS push in India.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ **Data-center buildout (Colo + Hyperscaler):** Cummins India direct beneficiary via QSK60/HHP gensets + dedicated DC aftermarket.
- ✅ **CPCB-IV+ out-of-warranty wave (Jun-2026 onward):** boosts distribution/aftermarket annuity.
- ⭐ **Parent's 20GW / $450m capacity add by 2030:** could shorten import lead-times → faster India DC fulfilment, but also enables imported 78/95L that may pressure local cost-edge.
- ⭐ **Solar-cell / pharma / quick-commerce / realty capex:** secondary powergen demand pools.

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.

themes.title: Capital-goods & machine-tool import-substitution
themes.need: Atmanirbhar machine-tool and heavy-engineering localization is supply-constrained against import-substituting demand. JYOTICNC runs >100% utilization with a INR4,732cr order book and near-triples capacity; ELGIEQUIP/CUMMINSIND/ELECON/LMW ride the same capex + export + China+1 pull; ISGEC/BHEL/GMMPFAUDLR/KIRLPNU on process + energy capex.
themes.driver: Capacity expansion going live (JYOTICNC); defence/EMS order conversion; US-reshoring export demand (ELGIEQUIP).

themes.title: Power generation & utilities - baseload + new capacity
themes.need: Record peak demand and a thermal+hydro+nuclear capacity-addition cycle underpin regulated and merchant generators plus their service chain. NTPC/JSWENERGY/TATAPOWER/TORNTPOWER/ADANIPOWER add thermal + RE; NHPC/SJVN/NLCINDIA on hydro/lignite; TRITURBINE/TDPOWERSYS/GVPIL on turbines/generators & aftermarket; POWERMECH on EPC + O&M.
themes.driver: Peak-demand/PLF strength; new-unit commissioning; FGD + thermal-aftermarket order conversion.

hero.oneLiner: Cummins India is a high-payout, net-cash market leader riding a structural domestic power-gen upcycle, with **data-center gensets (30–35% of domestic powergen)** as the marquee growth driver on top of CPCB-IV+ content gains, a fast-growing 20%+ distribution/aftermarket annuity, and a steady-but-cautious export book — guidance for FY27 is deliberately "moderate growth across segments" given commodity inflation and geopolitics.
